title: IndiGo to Discontinue All Widebody Operations, End Norse Atlantic Lease
excerpt: India's largest airline will switch Mumbai-Amsterdam to A321XLR and suspend London Heathrow service until its own Airbus A350s arrive, citing geopolitical disruptions.
body:
• IndiGo will discontinue all widebody operations from October 25 and end its damp lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways by October 31.
  • Mumbai-Amsterdam flights will switch to Airbus A321XLR aircraft, while London Heathrow service is suspended until the airline's own A350-900 fleet arrives.
  • The airline cited a challenging operating environment driven by geopolitical tensions, rising fuel costs, and severe airspace restrictions from the Middle East conflict.
  • IndiGo had leased six Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners from Norse Atlantic starting March 2025 to fast-track its long-haul ambitions.

End of the Widebody Experiment

IndiGo, India's largest airline by market share, announced on Friday that it would discontinue all widebody operations from October 25, concluding its damp lease agreement with Norwegian carrier Norse Atlantic Airways on October 31.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=FiyUBJQ3CrA

The decision marks a setback for IndiGo's ambitious push into long-haul markets, which began in March 2025 when it leased six Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners from Norse Atlantic to connect Indian cities with European destinations.

Route Restructuring

Under the new plan, IndiGo's Mumbai-Amsterdam flights will continue but will be operated using the narrowbody Airbus A321XLR, a long-range variant capable of covering the route with reduced capacity. Services to and from London Heathrow, however, will be temporarily suspended until the airline takes delivery of its own Airbus A350-900 aircraft.

The airline had already returned one of its six leased 787s to Norse Atlantic in August after closing its Manchester routes, citing longer flight times from airspace constraints and dramatically escalating costs.

"The response and support for these services have reinforced our belief in the opportunity for IndiGo's long-haul ambitions, and we are convinced that this discontinuation is temporary."

— Abhijit Dasgupta, SVP Network Planning, IndiGo

Geopolitics Derails Long-Haul Plans

IndiGo pointed to a challenging operating environment driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions as the primary factor behind its decision. The US-Iran conflict, which began in February 2026, has forced airlines to reroute flights around Iranian and Iraqi airspace, adding hours to journey times and significantly increasing fuel costs.

Rising aviation turbine fuel prices, severe airspace restrictions, and foreign exchange volatility have pushed operating costs well beyond what the airline originally planned when it launched its widebody services.

Norse Atlantic said the returned aircraft would be redeployed on routes between Europe and Thailand during the 2026-27 winter season. CEO Eivind Roald noted that the companies had jointly initiated a strategic collaboration project to assess deeper cooperation.

What It Means for Travelers

For the Indian diaspora in the UK, the suspension of London Heathrow service removes a direct connection that had proven popular since its launch. IndiGo had offered competitive fares on the route, challenging established carriers like Air India and British Airways.

The switch to A321XLR on the Amsterdam route means fewer seats per flight, which could push up fares during peak travel periods. However, IndiGo's own A350 fleet, once delivered, would give the airline widebody capability without the cost overhead of leasing from an external operator.

IndiGo remains committed to long-haul flying, framing the move as a temporary measure rather than a strategic retreat. The airline continues to operate other international routes and views its A350 order as the foundation for a sustainable widebody network.
nri_angle: Indian travelers in the US and UK face disruptions as IndiGo's ambitious long-haul expansion hits turbulence, with London Heathrow service suspended indefinitely and route changes affecting diaspora travel plans.
